brief.subject: PTINs expire Dec. 31: renewal season is open
brief.headline: Tax Preparers: Current PTINs Expire Dec. 31, 2026
brief.dek: PTIN renewals are due, the IRS posts a hearing notice on Trump account investment rules, and Chicago and NYC advance taxes on the wealthy.
brief.lede: Every paid preparer's PTIN runs out on Dec. 31, 2026. Renew before year-end to keep filing returns for clients without interruption.

sections.heading: PTIN Renewal Window Is Open
bullets: Current preparer tax identification numbers expire Dec. 31, 2026, so renewal is now on the year-end checklist.
Anyone paid to prepare returns needs a valid PTIN, and it must be renewed every year.
A lapsed PTIN could sideline preparers just as filing season approaches.

sections.heading: IRS Posts Hearing Notice on Trump Accounts
bullets: The IRS issued a hearing notice tied to proposed rules on eligible investments for Trump accounts.
The proposed regulations first appeared in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026.
The rules govern the only assets these accounts may hold before the year the beneficiary turns 18.
Advisers fielding family-savings questions should monitor how the final rules take shape.

sections.heading: Big Cities Push Taxes on the Wealthy
bullets: Chicago voters backed a millionaire tax in a non-binding referendum, and the mayor called it a mandate for tax-the-rich policies.
A Brooklyn appeals court reversed a lower court ruling, allowing New York City's pied-à-terre tax to move forward.
The ruling means the city does not have to restart the process, a key win for Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
Owners and clients with high incomes or second homes in these cities should watch for follow-up action.

items.snippet: A Brooklyn appeals court on Wednesday handed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani a key victory by reversing a lower court ruling that would have required the city to restart the process.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts; Hearing
items.snippet: This document provides a notice of proposed rulemaking (CC- 00349938-26) published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. The proposed regulations provided guidance regarding eligible investments, which are the only assets in which the Trump account may be invested before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains 18.
